summary: Burlington County, NJ lookout near Retreat with 1924-1947 newspaper items on its watchers; heights conflict (60 vs 90 ft); build date and fate not found.

events.note: A new watcher took a post at the look-out station near Retreat, which the state forestry service maintained for part of the year
Tower opened for the season with Clifford Prickitt in charge
Watchman Peter Curlis fell from the observation platform on December 16; the year is inferred from the February 1, 1932 item
William Hagerthey, 23, among the men who opened the lookout towers for the season; the item names him for the 60-foot Retreat tower
James Lawton was to man the tower; the item gives its height as 90 feet and places it in Southampton township woodlands

corrections.proposed: no height until the 60-foot and 90-foot figures are checked
corrections.why: 10.7 m is 35 feet, the same figure as the fall in the 1932 item, which suggests a number was carried over from the wrong line. The page gives 60 feet in 1940 and 90 feet in 1947.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The 1940 item gives a 60-foot tower and the 1947 item a 90-foot tower. The page does not say whether the tower was raised or rebuilt between those years, so the story gives both figures and picks neither.

notes_for_editor: One source only: a Forest Lookouts page that quotes 1924-1947 Courier-Post and Morning Post items. The page gives no build date and nothing on fate. Checked and empty: the Wikipedia NJ fire tower list (no Big Hill entry), the Wikipedia Retreat article (no tower mention), the NJFFS Division B page (current network only), and the FFLA New Jersey page (marked 'Under Construction'). Two web searches found nothing new. Before this story is treated as complete, look for a Burlington County or Southampton Township history source and the date the tower came down. The 10.7 m record height probably comes from the 35-foot fall figure.
